name: oss
description: Open Science Skills (oss). 43 Claude Code skills for experimental social science and computational text analysis. Orchestration and delegation: orchestrate (a multi-model workflow that detects whether the session runs Fable or Opus and takes the matching lead role, with --lead fable|opus to override), advisor (a working model escalates one decision point to Fable at max reasoning effort; not for a Fable session), spawn (full peer Claude Code sessions in their own git worktrees and terminal panes via herdr, tmux, or claude background agents, briefed by contract and merged back), model-committee (a deliberative GPT-6 Astra and Claude Opus committee chaired by a premier model that is never a member — Fable by default via /model-committee; /model-committee-astra, /model-committee-opus, /model-committee-sol select the others), model-council-voting, and diverge (brainstorm-then-select, with --codex delegating to GPT-6 Astra). Repo hygiene: sitrep (report where a project stands from its handoff files and live git state) and finished (record what changed into the project's handoff and log at session close). Research design: research-grill (a rounds-based interview that takes an idea to a falsifiable question, a question to a full design, or a draft to its reviewer objections; student-safe, credited to Matt Pocock's grill-me), research-wayfinder (decision-map planning across sessions, adapted from Pocock's wayfinder), hypothesis-building, survey-design, conjoint-design, conjoint-cleaning, conjoint-diagnostics, list-experiment, cross-national-design, pre-registration-writing, qualtrics-ops (live Qualtrics v3 operations plus a read-only pre-fielding audit mode; /survey-flow-audit is the alias), survey-data-audit. Text and documents: text-classification (including resumable batch pipelines and rule-based baselines), llm-calibration-logprobs, topic-modeling, doc-to-markdown, vlm-ocr (evaluate, run, clean; /vlm-ocr-evaluation, /vlm-ocr-pipeline, /post-ocr-cleanup are aliases), research-repo. Manuscript QA and reporting: citation-check, fact-check, literature-review, narrative-building, figures, tables, figure-table-audit, methods-reporting, paper-tex, replication-package (scaffold plus FAIR audit; /fair-check is the alias), paper-review-lite (with --codex cross-model mode; /paper-review-lite-codex is the alias), presubmit, journal-review (reviewer side), referee-response (author side: extract, order, and format the response to reviewers without writing the science). Deliverable pipeline: deliverable-open (a rounds interview that writes deliverable.yml, an append-only HANDOFF.md, a numbered planning/ wiki, an inbox/ for dictated braindumps, and for a talk the house deck template), deliverable-intake (captures into a wiki diff, every line classified and traced, decisions applied only on assent), and deliverable-lint (the whole-deliverable editorial review, detection only, deterministic gate first, one cheap finder per section, one strong-model global pass, adjudicated findings with anchors and honest NOT-CHECKED coverage under a dollar budget). Invoke as /oss:skill-name (or /skill-name when unambiguous). Every skill is on demand. None auto-triggers from context, so the library costs a session nothing until a skill is invoked by name.
